quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #17
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If your turn signals fail, what should you use to show you are turning?

options.text: Your horn
Your headlights
Hand signals
Your emergency flashers

questions.correctAnswerText: Hand signals
questions.explanation: If your turn signals do not work, use hand signals to tell other drivers you are turning.

questions.question: A driver age 21 or older cannot drive if they have at least ____ nanograms of THC per milliliter of blood.

options.text: Zero nanograms
One nanogram
Three nanograms
Five nanograms

questions.correctAnswerText: Five nanograms
questions.explanation: Drivers age 21 or older cannot drive with five nanograms or more of THC per milliliter of blood. Drivers under 21 cannot drive with any THC in their blood. Marijuana impairs your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line in the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers can pass when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Drivers can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers cannot pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Solid lines mean you cannot pass.

questions.question: What does this sign warn drivers about?

options.text: The right lane ends. Traffic must merge left.
The road curves ahead.
An intersection is coming.
Road construction ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane ends. Traffic must merge left.
questions.explanation: This sign means the right lane will end. Drivers in that lane must merge to the left.

questions.question: Which statement about drowsy drivers is true?

options.text: They should drink strong black coffee to stay awake.
They can drive so poorly that they seem drunk.
They can stay alert by opening a window and turning up the radio.
They are usually older drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can drive so poorly that they seem drunk.
questions.explanation: Drowsy drivers can drive as badly as drunk drivers. Opening a window, playing the radio, or drinking coffee is not enough to keep a drowsy driver alert.

questions.question: When backing up, you should:

options.text: Use only your mirrors.
Flash your lights.
Open your door to see if it is safe.
Turn your head and look through the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Always check behind your vehicle before backing. Small children and objects are hard to see from the driver's seat. Turn your head to look through the rear window. Do not rely only on mirrors.

questions.question: At night, how should you look if oncoming headlights are too bright?

options.text: Straight ahead.
Over your shoulder.
At the center of the road.
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming headlights are bright, look at the right edge of the road. Do not look directly at the headlights, as the glare can blind you for several seconds.

questions.question: If two vehicles reach a four-way stop at the same time, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.
Drivers should use hand signals to communicate.
One driver should proceed without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, vehicles go in the order they arrive. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the one on the left must let the one on the right go first.

questions.question: Another driver is passing your car. What should you do?

options.text: Pull off the road.
Signal when it is safe for them to pass.
Check for oncoming traffic and slow down to help them pass safely.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for oncoming traffic and slow down to help them pass safely.
questions.explanation: Stay to the right when another driver passes you. Check for oncoming traffic and slow down to make it easier for them to pass and return to your lane.

questions.question: How should you enter a freeway?

options.text: Signal, yield to traffic, and match the speed of traffic.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must yield to you.
Drive slowly to check traffic.
Always come to a complete stop first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, yield to traffic, and match the speed of traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging onto a freeway, signal and enter at the same speed as traffic. Always yield to other drivers already on the freeway.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving on a wet road?

options.text: Faster speeds make your tires less effective.
Water does not affect cars with good tires.
Deep water is safer than shallow water.
Slower speeds make the road more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: Faster speeds make your tires less effective.
questions.explanation: When you drive faster on wet roads, your tires cannot remove water from the road as well. If you go too fast, your tires lose grip and you will hydroplane (slide on a layer of water).

questions.question: To safely pass a bicycle, you should:

options.text: Honk to let the cyclist know you are passing.
Drive in the bicycle lane to pass them.
Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
Speed up and pull in front of them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: When passing a cyclist, slow down and give them plenty of space. Cyclists have less protection than drivers. Passing them too quickly can cause them to lose control.

questions.question: A first DUI conviction can result in license suspension for at least ____ if you refuse a breath test.

options.text: 30 days
90 days
One year
Two years

questions.correctAnswerText: One year
questions.explanation: If you refuse a breath test on your first DUI arrest, your license will be revoked for one year. A regular first DUI suspension is 90 days.

questions.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle, you should:

options.text: Stop right away and let it pass.
Move to the right side of the road as safely as you can and stop.
Slow down and let the vehicle pass.
Move slowly to the right and keep going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road as safely as you can and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle uses lights or sirens, move as far right as possible and stop. Do not stop in an intersection. This applies regardless of which direction the vehicle is coming from.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Steep downgrade ahead.
Crossroad ahead.
No right turn.
Narrow bridge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep downgrade ahead.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you a steep hill is coming. Slow down to protect your brakes and avoid accidents.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Do not drink and drive.
The road is slippery when wet.
Road curves ahead.
A hill is coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road becomes slippery when wet.

questions.question: When you are in a travel lane:

options.text: You may stop to drop off passengers.
You may stop to look up an address.
You may back up or make a U-turn if you miss a freeway exit.
Do not stop for any reason. Keep driving until you can safely pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not stop for any reason. Keep driving until you can safely pull off the road.
questions.explanation: Never stop in a travel lane. Keep moving until you can safely leave the road. If you miss your exit, go to the next one or find a safe place to turn around. Do not back up.

questions.question: To prevent hydroplaning, you should:

options.text: Keep your tires' tread depth good.
Keep your tires at the right air pressure.
Slow down when driving in rain.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, keep your tires in good condition with proper tread and air pressure. Also slow down when it rains. Hydroplaning happens most often at high speeds.

questions.question: Always use your turn signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal whenever you move left or right. Signal when leaving a parking space, changing lanes, or passing another vehicle.

questions.question: When you approach a railroad crossing with no warning lights or gates, you should:

options.text: Cross the tracks right away, as quickly as possible.
Always stop before crossing.
Be ready to yield to any train at the crossing.
Speed up to cross before a train arrives.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield to any train at the crossing.
questions.explanation: Always be prepared to yield to trains at crossings without lights or gates. Only cross when the entire vehicle can fit on the other side. Do not shift gears while crossing because your vehicle could stall.

questions.question: Before entering a roundabout, you must slow down and yield to:

options.text: Vehicles in the roundabout.
Bicyclists in the roundabout.
Pedestrians in the roundabout.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, you must yield to all pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout.

questions.question: When driving where children are playing, you should expect them to:

options.text: Know when it is safe to cross the street.
Stop at the curb before crossing the street.
Run out in front of you without looking.
Not cross the street unless they are with an adult.

questions.correctAnswerText: Run out in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Always slow down and be extra careful when children are near. Children may not understand danger and can run in front of your vehicle without looking.

questions.question: A good defensive driver:

options.text: Drives slowly at all times.
Watches what other drivers do.
Travels at a constant speed.
Only drives in familiar areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watches what other drivers do.
questions.explanation: All drivers can become distracted. A defensive driver watches what other drivers do and prepares for possible problems.

questions.question: When driving at high speeds, stay at least this distance behind the vehicle in front of you to stop safely in emergencies:

options.text: One second behind.
Four seconds behind.
Two seconds behind.
Ten seconds behind.

questions.correctAnswerText: Four seconds behind.
questions.explanation: At speeds of 30 mph or slower, two to three seconds is enough to stop safely. At higher speeds, keep four seconds between you and the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: Highway hypnosis can result from:

options.text: Staring at the road for long periods of time.
Taking frequent rest stops.
Getting too much sleep before your trip.
Taking short trips on expressways.

questions.correctAnswerText: Staring at the road for long periods of time.
questions.explanation: Highway hypnosis happens when you stare straight ahead for a long time and stop looking around your vehicle. This causes you to zone out and may cause you to crash into traffic that is slowing or stopping.
